hints: Focus on where astatine sits in Group 17 and how reactivity, oxidising power and reducing power change going down the group.
Recall that AgCl dissolves in dilute ammonia but AgI does not, and that a more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive one from its salt.
Think about what concentrated sulfuric acid does to NaBr and NaI, and predict what an even stronger reducing agent like At- would give.
walkthrough:
**Recall the Group 17 trends**

Astatine is below iodine, so it is the least reactive halogen here. That means $At_2$ is the weakest oxidising agent, but $At^-$ is the strongest reducing agent.

Trend down Group 17:
$$\text{oxidising power: } Cl_2 > Br_2 > I_2 > At_2$$
$$\text{reducing power: } Cl^- < Br^- < I^- < At^-$$

**Check solubility and displacement rules**

Silver halides get less soluble down the group. $AgCl$ dissolves in dilute $NH_3$, $AgBr$ only partly dissolves, $AgI$ is insoluble. So $AgAt$ will be even more insoluble.

Also, a halogen can only displace a halogen below it. So $At_2$ below chlorine cannot displace $Cl_2$ from $KCl$.

**Check reaction with sulfuric acid**

Concentrated $H_2SO_4$ oxidises halides, and the oxidation gets easier down the group.
$$NaCl \rightarrow HCl$$
$$NaBr \rightarrow Br_2$$
$$NaI \rightarrow I_2$$
Since $At^-$ is an even stronger reducing agent than $I^-$, it will certainly be oxidised to $At_2$. Dilute acid forming unstable $HAt(g)$ is very unlikely.

options.A: Incorrect. Solubility of AgX in ammonia decreases down Group 17. AgCl is soluble in dilute ammonia, AgI is insoluble, so AgAt, which is even less soluble, will not form a soluble complex.
options.B: Incorrect. This is the wrong way round for halogen displacement. Chlorine is above astatine and is more reactive, so astatine cannot displace chlorine from KCl. If anything, chlorine would displace astatine from KAt.
options.C: Incorrect. HAt is extremely unstable and a very strong reducing agent, so it would not be isolated as HAt(g) like HCl. At- would be oxidised rather than simply protonated, especially as we go down the group.
options.D: Correct. Concentrated sulfuric acid is an oxidising agent toward good reducing agents. Since Br- is oxidised to Br2 and I- to I2, At- which is an even stronger reducing agent will be oxidised to astatine, At2.
